key_insight: A ‘carbon-taxed’ compression pipeline that injects carbon/energy cost into compression objectives lets you shrink and accelerate overgrown language models while explicitly minimizing CO2 emissions alongside latency and memory.
problem_solved: Overgrown LLMs used in software engineering are large, slow to deploy, memory-intensive, and carbon-heavy; the paper addresses how to compress them so they remain useful but far cheaper and greener to run.
method: Introduce a carbon-aware objective (a 'carbon tax' signal or penalty) that biases compression decisions toward lower-energy operations and deployments.
Apply a staged green-compression pipeline—carbon-guided pruning, reference-aware distillation, and budgeted quantization—optimizing for accuracy under combined compute/memory/carbon budgets.
Automated budgeted selection: map deployment constraints (latency, memory, carbon) to a recommended compressed checkpoint and quantization strategy.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to deploy smaller, faster LLMs with measurable reductions in energy use and carbon footprint while preserving task performance—supporting scalable, cost-effective, and sustainable model deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing stages (analysis → carbon-taxed pruning → distillation → quantization → deployment) with carbon/compute icons at each step
Trade-off visualization (accuracy vs compute vs CO2e) — e.g., 2D contour or 3-axis plot showing pareto frontier
Before/after bar charts comparing model size, inference latency, and estimated CO2 emissions
Interactive budget selector mockup (sliders for latency, memory, carbon) that outputs a compression recipe
paper_title: Carbon-Taxed Transformers: A Green Compression Pipeline for Overgrown Language Models
paper_authors: Ajmain Inqiad Alam, Palash Roy, Chanchal K. Roy, Banani Roy, Kevin A. Schneider
